Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_path="C:\\inetpub\\pub\\*" (Processes.process_name IN ("schtask.exe","schtask2.exe") OR Processes.process_name="*_update.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_path="C:\\inetpub\\pub\\*" (Processes.process_name IN ("schtask.exe","schtask2.exe") OR Processes.process_name="*_update.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Sandworm SOCKS5 C2 egress to 31.172.71[.]5 (Fornex) or progamevl.ru AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts outbound network connections to the SOCKS5 server (31.172.71.5, Fornex Hosting) and the C2 domain progamevl.ru attributed to the DynoWiper / Sandworm infrastructure. Detection is independent of the wiper executing — captures earlier-stage tunnelling. Rationale: 31.172.71[.]5 (Fornex Hosting SOCKS5, first seen 2024-10-27) and progamevl.ru are the only network IOCs the article supplies. Both are attributed to the Sandworm infrastructure for this campaign — any traffic from the corporate estate to these is investigatable on sight.
ATT&CKT1090 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel researcher's lab box deliberately probing the IOC
  • Open-source intelligence collector pulling WHOIS / passive DNS
  • Sinkhole / honeypot infrastructure inside the corporate range
  • Mis-attributed shared-hosting tenant (Fornex hosts other unrelated sites on the same IP — verify domain/SNI before high-severity)
Response runbook
1. Triage: confirm the host is not a known TI sandbox; pull the initiating process and user; check whether the connection succeeded (bytes transferred / status). 2. Contain: black-hole 31.172.71.5 and progamevl.ru at the perimeter / EDR network-block; isolate the originating host; reset the user's credentials. 3. Hunt: search 90 days backwards across DNS, firewall and proxy logs for the same indicators; look for SOCKS5-shape traffic (TCP/1080 or non-standard ports) from any host that previously touched 31.172.71.5; pivot to identify any binary on disk on those hosts matching the DynoWiper hash set.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(90d)
| where RemoteIP == "31.172.71.5" or RemoteUrl has "progamevl.ru"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Protocol, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(
  CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
  | where DestinationIP == "31.172.71.5" or RequestURL has "progamevl.ru" or DestinationHostName has "progamevl.ru"
  | project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, SourceIP, SourceUserName, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, DestinationHostName, RequestURL
),
(
  DnsEvents
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
  | where Name has "progamevl.ru"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, Result
),
(
  ImNetworkSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
  | where DstIpAddr == "31.172.71.5" or DstHostname has "progamevl.ru"
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, DstHostname, Url
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Sandworm DynoWiper C2 Egress to 31.172.71[.]5 or progamevl.ru
id: 1a8c4f2e-6d7b-4a3c-9e1f-5d8b2c7a4e1f
description: Detects outbound traffic or DNS resolution to the Sandworm DynoWiper SOCKS5 C2 (31.172.71.5) and domain progamevl.ru documented by ESET.
references:

logsource:

detection:

  selection_domain:

  condition: selection_ip or selection_domain
level: critical
(source:(windows.sysmon OR crowdstrike OR zeek OR firewall) AND (CIDR(@network.destination.ip, 31.172.71.5/32) OR @DestinationIp:31.172.71.5 OR @dns.question.name:*progamevl.ru OR @DestinationHostname:*progamevl.ru OR @url.domain:*progamevl.ru))
(#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 RemoteAddressIP4="31.172.71.5") OR (#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/progamevl\.ru$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RemoteAddressIP4, DomainName], function=count())
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest_ip="31.172.71.5" OR All_Traffic.dest="*progamevl.ru" OR All_Traffic.app="*progamevl.ru*") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.src_ip All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_ip All_Traffic.dest_port All_Traffic.app All_Traffic.user | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest_ip="31.172.71.5" OR All_Traffic.dest="*progamevl.ru" OR All_Traffic.app="*progamevl.ru*") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.src_ip All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_ip All_Traffic.dest_port All_Traffic.app All_Traffic.user | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Mass file-content overwrite by single non-system process from non-standard path AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the DynoWiper impact phase — the wiper overwrites file content with a 16-byte buffer of random data generated once at start of execution. Detects a single non-system, non-Program-Files process touching an unusually high count of distinct files within a short window. Rationale: Article specifies DynoWiper's destructive phase overwrites every reachable file content with a 16-byte random buffer; the resulting telemetry shape is one process emitting hundreds-to-thousands of FileModified events in seconds. Excluding C:\Windows\ and C:\Program Files anchors the hunt away from updaters/installers.
ATT&CKT1485 T1561.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Veeam / Commvault / NetBackup running a large incremental backup that rewrites timestamps
  • Robocopy / xcopy bulk file migration during a server move
  • Code-signing or DRM tool re-stamping a large content library
  • Build server emitting hundreds of artefacts into a workspace
  • Disk encryption rollout (BitLocker, Symantec PGP) re-writing files at scale
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("veeam.backup.shell.exe","robocopy.exe","xcopy.exe","MsMpEng.exe","WindowsDefender.exe","bcdedit.exe","manage-bde.exe","MBAMAgent.exe","OneDrive.exe","FileCoAuth.exe","backup.exe")
Response runbook
1. Triage: confirm the process image is unsigned or signed by an unexpected publisher; check whether the source is in the DynoWiper hash set; collect SHA-256 and a sample of overwritten file paths. 2. Contain: kill the process, isolate the host, and pause shadow-copy deletion / VSS shrink jobs to preserve recoverable state. 3. Hunt: search across the domain for the same process image / hash; correlate with the C:\inetpub\pub\ drop detection and 31.172.71.5 C2 detection; identify lateral-movement source by joining initiating-process logon-session to DeviceLogonEvents.
let WindowMinutes = 5m;
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileModified","FileCreated")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith @"C:\Windows\"
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith @"C:\Program Files"
| summarize FileCount = dcount(FolderPath), SampleFiles = make_set(FolderPath, 20), SampleProc = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
    by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessId, bin(Timestamp, WindowMinutes)
| where FileCount > 200
| order by Timestamp desc
let WindowMinutes = 5m;
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileModified","FileCreated")
| where isnotempty(ActingProcessName)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where not(ActingProcessName startswith @"C:\Windows\")
| where not(ActingProcessName startswith @"C:\Program Files")
| summarize FileCount = dcount(TargetFilePath), SampleFiles = make_set(TargetFilePath, 20), SampleCmd = any(ActingProcessCommandLine)
    by DvcHostname, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessId, bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMinutes)
| where FileCount > 200
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 -@Image:(C:\\Windows\\* OR C:\\Program\ Files* OR c:\\windows\\* OR c:\\program\ files*)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/^[cC]:\\Windows\\/
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/^[cC]:\\Program Files/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, ContextProcessId], function=count(as=FileCount))
| FileCount > 200
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` dc(Filesystem.file_path) as FileCount values(Filesystem.file_path) as Files min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","written") Filesystem.process_path!="C:\\Windows\\*" Filesystem.process_path!="C:\\Program Files*" by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.process_path Filesystem.user span=5m | where FileCount > 200 | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false dc(Filesystem.file_path) as FileCount values(Filesystem.file_path) as Files min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","written") Filesystem.process_path!="C:\\Windows\\*" Filesystem.process_path!="C:\\Program Files*" by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.process_path Filesystem.user span=5m | where FileCount > 200 | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("31.172.71.5") or RemoteUrl has_any ("progamevl.ru")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic(["31.172.71.5"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["progamevl.ru"]);
ImNetworkSession

| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")

| where files > 200

       Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_path
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| append [
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("created","modified")
      AND (Filesystem.file_path="*C:\inetpub\pub\*" OR Filesystem.file_name IN ("schtask.exe","schtask2.exe","_update.exe","rubeus.exe","tmp_backup.tmp.exe","ts_5wb.tmp.exe","rsocx.exe"))
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, Filesystem.process_name,

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] GhostChat C2/staging infrastructure contact (hitpak.org, buildthenations.info, fkclb.com)
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
GhostChat C2/staging infrastructure contact (hitpak.org, buildthenations.info, fkclb.com) AICommand & Control High
Hunts any endpoint resolving or contacting the GhostChat / ClickFix campaign infrastructure tied to the Pakistan-targeted spyware operation. While the Android payload itself won't show on EDR, the same actor's ClickFix attack delivers a Windows implant that beacons to the same C2 estate, so DNS/proxy hits on these domains from Windows hosts are high-confidence pivots. Rationale: Domains hitpak.org, buildthenations.info, and fkclb.com are the dual-use C2/staging hosts shared between the Android GhostChat payload and the same actor's ClickFix Windows implant per ESET's writeup; any Windows endpoint contact is anomalous because the brand impersonates a Pakistani government site and has no legitimate enterprise use. Cross-checked with WeLiveSecurity blog and ESET telemetry tags. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/love-actually-fake-dating-app-used-lure-targeted-spyware-campaign-pakistan/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004 T1583.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel analyst manually browsing the IOC for triage
  • Sandbox detonation environment resolving the domain
  • Researcher running enrichment lookups via VirusTotal/Shodan that proxy through endpoint
  • Web filter test traffic with the IOC in a watchlist
  • Pakistani diaspora users genuinely visiting impersonated gov site
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msedge.exe","chrome.exe","firefox.exe") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("--headless","sandbox","detonation")
Response runbook
Step 1 (Triage): Identify the originating user, host role, and process. Pull the full URL, referrer, and the surrounding 5 minutes of process activity — confirm whether the request came from a browser (likely ClickFix lure) or a non-browser process (likely implant beacon). Check Defender/Falcon for any process-tree branching from this contact. Step 2 (Contain): Block the three domains at proxy/DNS sinkhole; isolate the host via Defender Live Response or Falcon RTR if a non-browser process initiated the connection; reset the user's WhatsApp web sessions and AAD credentials. Step 3 (Hunt): Pivot on the host for ClickFix patterns (mshta/powershell launched with a clipboard-pasted command in the last 24h), look for WhatsApp web device-linking from unfamiliar IPs for the same user, and sweep the org's mobile MDM for sideloaded APKs named 'GhostChat' or with matching package signatures.
let GhostChatDomains = dynamic(["hitpak.org","buildthenations.info","fkclb.com"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (GhostChatDomains) or RemoteUrl endswith ".hitpak.org" or RemoteUrl endswith ".buildthenations.info" or RemoteUrl endswith ".fkclb.com"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
let GhostChatDomains = dynamic(["hitpak.org","buildthenations.info","fkclb.com"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (DnsEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Name has_any (GhostChatDomains) or Name endswith ".hitpak.org" or Name endswith ".buildthenations.info" or Name endswith ".fkclb.com"
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=Computer, ClientIP, Domain=Name, QueryType=QueryTypeName, Source="DnsEvents"),
  (CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where RequestURL has_any (GhostChatDomains) or DestinationHostName has_any (GhostChatDomains)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=coalesce(SourceHostName, DeviceExternalID), ClientIP=SourceIP, Domain=coalesce(DestinationHostName, RequestURL), QueryType=DeviceAction, Source="CommonSecurityLog"),
  (ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Url has_any (GhostChatDomains) or DstHostname has_any (GhostChatDomains)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=SrcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, Domain=coalesce(DstHostname, HttpHostName), QueryType=HttpMethod, Source="ImWebSession")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

GhostChat C2 beacon URL pattern: hitpak.org/page.php?tynor=<host>sss<user> AIexfil High
Detects the exact GhostChat / ClickFix C2 beacon URL template observed by ESET, where the malware exfiltrates host+username via the tynor query parameter delimited by the literal string 'sss'. This URL shape is unique to the campaign and is not used by any legitimate web service. Rationale: The URL template `/page.php?tynor=<host>sss<user>` is a malware-specific exfiltration shape — the literal token `tynor` and the `sss` delimiter between the two encoded fields are unique strings called out by ESET. Combining the template with the three known C2 domains gives near-zero false-positive rate. Cross-referenced via ESET WeLiveSecurity blog. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/love-actually-fake-dating-app-used-lure-targeted-spyware-campaign-pakistan/
ATT&CKT1041 T1071.001 T1567
Data sourcesWeb.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel researcher submitting the IOC URL to a sandbox or curl test
  • WAF/DLP appliance generating a synthetic test request
  • Red-team exercise replaying ESET's published IOC for table-top
  • Honeypot relay capturing the same beacon
  • DFIR replay of a captured pcap
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("curl.exe","wget.exe","powershell.exe") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has_any ("test","validate","sandbox")
Response runbook
Step 1 (Triage): Decode the tynor parameter to recover the victim's hostname and username — the format is `tynor=<HOSTNAME>sss<USERNAME>`. Validate the host actually exists in the asset inventory and that the username matches an AAD identity. Pull the originating process for the network connection. Step 2 (Contain): Isolate the host immediately (Defender 'Isolate device' / Falcon network containment), force-revoke the user's AAD sessions and WhatsApp linked devices, and block the three C2 domains plus the resolved IPs at egress. Step 3 (Hunt): Sweep the org for any other host that has resolved hitpak.org/buildthenations.info/fkclb.com in the last 90 days; review the user's mobile device fleet for sideloaded APKs (GhostChat package); check for ClickFix entry vector by looking for clipboard-pasted PowerShell/mshta executions on the host in the 24h before the beacon.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl matches regex @"(?i)(hitpak\.org|buildthenations\.info|fkclb\.com)/page\.php\?tynor=[^&]*sss[^&]*"
   or RemoteUrl has "page.php?tynor=" and RemoteUrl has "sss"
| extend BeaconHost = extract(@"(?i)tynor=([^s&]+)sss", 1, RemoteUrl)
| extend BeaconUser = extract(@"(?i)sss([^&]+)", 1, RemoteUrl)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, BeaconHost, BeaconUser
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where (RequestURL matches regex @"(?i)(hitpak\.org|buildthenations\.info|fkclb\.com)/page\.php\?tynor=[^&]*sss[^&]*")
         or (RequestURL has "page.php?tynor=" and RequestURL has "sss")
    | extend BeaconHost = extract(@"(?i)tynor=([^s&]+)sss", 1, RequestURL)
    | extend BeaconUser = extract(@"(?i)sss([^&]+)", 1, RequestURL)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=coalesce(SourceHostName, DeviceExternalID), ClientIP=SourceIP, User=coalesce(SourceUserName, AccountName), URL=RequestURL, UA=RequestClientApplication, BeaconHost, BeaconUser, Source="CommonSecurityLog"),
  (ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where (Url matches regex @"(?i)(hitpak\.org|buildthenations\.info|fkclb\.com)/page\.php\?tynor=[^&]*sss[^&]*")
         or (Url has "page.php?tynor=" and Url has "sss")
    | extend BeaconHost = extract(@"(?i)tynor=([^s&]+)sss", 1, Url)
    | extend BeaconUser = extract(@"(?i)sss([^&]+)", 1, Url)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=SrcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, User=SrcUsername, URL=Url, UA=HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, BeaconHost, BeaconUser, Source="ImWebSession"),
  (W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where csUriStem endswith "page.php" and csUriQuery has "tynor=" and csUriQuery has "sss"
    | extend BeaconHost = extract(@"(?i)tynor=([^s&]+)sss", 1, csUriQuery)
    | extend BeaconUser = extract(@"(?i)sss([^&]+)", 1, csUriQuery)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=Computer, ClientIP=cIP, User=csUserName, URL=strcat(csUriStem, "?", csUriQuery), UA=csUserAgent, BeaconHost, BeaconUser, Source="W3CIISLog")
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: GhostChat C2 Beacon URL Pattern (tynor + sss Delimiter)
id: a14d70e2-9b88-4f31-bd2f-5e8af6d31cc1
description: Detects the GhostChat / ClickFix Pakistan campaign's distinctive C2 beacon URL where the payload exfils hostname+username via /page.php?tynor=<host>sss<user> on infrastructure hitpak.org, buildthenations.info, or fkclb.com.
references:
  - https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/love-actually-fake-dating-app-used-lure-targeted-spyware-campaign-pakistan/

(source:windows.sysmon OR source:windows.defender OR source:linux.auditd OR source:zscaler OR source:paloalto OR source:fortinet) @http.url:(*page.php?tynor=*sss* OR *hitpak.org/page.php* OR *buildthenations.info/page.php* OR *fkclb.com/page.php*)
(#event_simpleName=DnsRequest OR #event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 OR #event_simpleName=HttpRequest)
| regex("page\\.php\\?tynor=[^&]+sss", field=HttpUrl) OR regex("(hitpak\\.org|buildthenations\\.info|fkclb\\.com)", field=DomainName)
| HttpUrl=/page\.php\?tynor=[^&]+sss/i OR (DomainName=/(hitpak\.org|buildthenations\.info|fkclb\.com)/i AND HttpUrl=/page\.php/i)

WEB

| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.url) as url from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.url="*page.php?tynor=*sss*" by Web.src Web.user Web.dest Web.http_user_agent | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```

    from datamodel=Web

| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`

| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",

         by Processes.dest, Processes.user

Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High
Browser-pasted PowerShell launched from explorer/Run dialog — ClickFix social engineering.
ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.001

DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

DynoWiper deployment from shared inetpub\pub directory (Sandworm, Poland Dec 2025) AIInstallation High
Hunts for the three DynoWiper SHA-1s and their staging filenames (schtask.exe, schtask2.exe, *_update.exe) executing from or being written to a shared directory. ESET observed the wiper deployed to C:\inetpub\pub\ on the victim domain on 29 Dec 2025 and run directly from that share rather than via GPO push. Rationale: Uses the three SHA-1s ESET published (4EC3C9..., 86596A..., 69EDE7...), the unusual staging directory C:\inetpub\pub\ where Sandworm dropped the binaries, and the masquerading filenames schtask.exe/schtask2.exe (impersonating Windows schtasks.exe). All three pivots are confirmed by the ESET technical follow-up and BleepingComputer coverage. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/dynowiper-update-technical-analysis-attribution/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/sandworm-hackers-linked-to-failed-wiper-attack-on-polands-energy-systems/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/01/new-dynowiper-malware-used-in-attempted.html
ATT&CKT1485 T1036.005 T1021.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
let DynoWiperSHA1 = dynamic(["4EC3C90846AF6B79EE1A5188EEFA3FD21F6D4CF6","86596A5C5B05A8BFBD14876DE7404702F7D0D61B","69EDE7E341FD26FA0577692B601D80CB44778D93"]);
union isfuzzy=true
( DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where SHA1 in~ (DynoWiperSHA1)
       or InitiatingProcessSHA1 in~ (DynoWiperSHA1)
       or (FolderPath has @"\inetpub\pub\" and FileName endswith ".exe" and FileName !in~ ("w3wp.exe","appcmd.exe"))
       or (FileName in~ ("schtask.exe","schtask2.exe") and FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Windows\")
       or (FileName endswith "_update.exe" and FolderPath has @"\inetpub\")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA1,
              ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
),
( DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where SHA1 in~ (DynoWiperSHA1)
       or (FolderPath has @"\inetpub\pub\" and FileName endswith ".exe" and ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified"))
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA1,
              ProcessCommandLine="(file_event)", InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
)
| order by Timestamp desc
let DynoWiperSHA1 = dynamic(["4EC3C90846AF6B79EE1A5188EEFA3FD21F6D4CF6","86596A5C5B05A8BFBD14876DE7404702F7D0D61B","69EDE7E341FD26FA0577692B601D80CB44778D93"]);
union isfuzzy=true
( SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where FileHash has_any (DynoWiperSHA1)
       or (NewProcessName endswith "\\schtask.exe" and NewProcessName !contains "\\System32\\")
       or NewProcessName endswith "\\schtask2.exe"
       or NewProcessName matches regex @"(?i)\\inetpub\\pub\\[^\\]+\.exe$"
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, FileHash
),
( ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where TargetFileSHA1 in~ (DynoWiperSHA1)
       or (TargetFilePath has @"\inetpub\pub\" and TargetFileName endswith ".exe")
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, Account=ActorUsername,
              NewProcessName=TargetFilePath, CommandLine=ActingProcessCommandLine,
              ParentProcessName=ActingProcessName, FileHash=TargetFileSHA1
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: DynoWiper Execution - Sandworm Polish Energy Sector Attack (Dec 2025)
id: 9f3a2c1b-7d4e-4a51-8e62-1d5b3f9c4a87
description: Detects execution of the DynoWiper data-wiper used by Sandworm against a Polish energy company on 29 Dec 2025, by SHA-1 hash and the staging filenames/paths observed by ESET.
references:
    - https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/eset-research-sandworm-cyberattack-poland-power-grid-late-2025/
    - https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/dynowiper-update-technical-analysis-attribution/
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/03
tags:
    - attack.t1485
    - attack.t1036.005
    - attack.g0034
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_hash:
        Hashes|contains:
            - 'SHA1=4EC3C90846AF6B79EE1A5188EEFA3FD21F6D4CF6'
            - 'SHA1=86596A5C5B05A8BFBD14876DE7404702F7D0D61B'
            - 'SHA1=69EDE7E341FD26FA0577692B601D80CB44778D93'
    selection_path:
        Image|contains: '\inetpub\pub\'
        Image|endswith: '.exe'
    selection_name:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\schtask.exe'
            - '\schtask2.exe'
    filter_legit_iis:
        Image|endswith: '\w3wp.exe'
    filter_legit_schtasks:
        Image|contains: '\Windows\System32\'
    condition: (selection_hash or selection_path or (selection_name and not filter_legit_schtasks)) and not filter_legit_iis
falsepositives:
    - Highly unlikely; legitimate IIS content directories are usually \inetpub\wwwroot, not \inetpub\pub. Verify if a custom IIS site uses that path.
level: critical

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_hash IN ("4ec3c90846af6b79ee1a5188eefa3fd21f6d4cf6","86596a5c5b05a8bfbd14876de7404702f7d0d61b","69ede7e341fd26fa0577692b601d80cb44778d93") OR (Processes.process_name IN ("schtask.exe","schtask2.exe") AND NOT Processes.process_path IN ("*\\Windows\\System32\\*","*\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\*")) OR (Processes.process_path="*\\inetpub\\pub\\*" AND Processes.process_name!="w3wp.exe")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process_path Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)` | append [ | tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_hash IN ("4ec3c90846af6b79ee1a5188eefa3fd21f6d4cf6","86596a5c5b05a8bfbd14876de7404702f7d0d61b","69ede7e341fd26fa0577692b601d80cb44778d93") OR (Filesystem.file_path="*\\inetpub\\pub\\*" AND Filesystem.file_name="*.exe") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` ]
rsocx SOCKS5 reverse proxy beacon to 31.172.71.5:8008 (Sandworm Poland C2) AICommand & Control High
Hunts for the rsocx tunnelling tool Sandworm staged in the Polish energy intrusion: a binary executed from a user Downloads folder with the argument '-r 31.172.71.5:8008', and any host-to-IP egress to 31.172.71.5 (Fornex Hosting). The combination of cmdline shape + IP is unique to this campaign. Rationale: Anchors on the exact rsocx cmdline syntax 'r.exe -r 31.172.71.5:8008' and the C2 IP 31.172.71.5 (Fornex Hosting) ESET published in the technical follow-up. Both the Downloads-folder staging path and the unusual port 8008 give a near-zero FP profile. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/dynowiper-update-technical-analysis-attribution/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/sandworm-hackers-linked-to-failed-wiper-attack-on-polands-energy-systems/
ATT&CKT1090.001 T1090.002 T1572
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
let SandwormProxyIP = "31.172.71.5";
let SandwormProxyPort = 8008;
union isfuzzy=true
( DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has SandwormProxyIP
       or ProcessCommandLine has "31.172.71.5:8008"
       or (FileName =~ "r.exe" and FolderPath has @"\Downloads\" and ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\s-r\s+\d{1,3}(\.\d{1,3}){3}:8008\b")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
              SHA1, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP="", RemotePort=int(null)
),
( DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where RemoteIP == SandwormProxyIP
       or (RemotePort == SandwormProxyPort and InitiatingProcessFolderPath has @"\Downloads\")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName,
              FileName=InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath=InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
              ProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA1=InitiatingProcessSHA1,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort
)
| order by Timestamp desc
let SandwormProxyIP = "31.172.71.5";
let SandwormProxyPort = 8008;
union isfuzzy=true
( SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where CommandLine has SandwormProxyIP
       or CommandLine has "31.172.71.5:8008"
       or (NewProcessName endswith "\\Downloads\\r.exe" and CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\s-r\s+\d{1,3}(\.\d{1,3}){3}:8008\b")
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
),
( CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DestinationIP == SandwormProxyIP
       or (DestinationPort == SandwormProxyPort and (Activity has "allow" or DeviceAction has "allow"))
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer=SourceHostName, Account=SourceUserName,
              NewProcessName=SourceProcessName, CommandLine=Message, ParentProcessName="",
              SrcIP=SourceIP, DstIP=DestinationIP, DstPort=DestinationPort
),
( ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DstIpAddr == SandwormProxyIP
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, Account=SrcUsername,
              NewProcessName=ProcessName, CommandLine="", ParentProcessName="",
              SrcIP=SrcIpAddr, DstIP=DstIpAddr, DstPort=DstPortNumber
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

description: Detects execution of the rsocx SOCKS5 reverse-proxy used by Sandworm in the Dec 2025 attack on a Polish energy company. The C2 IP 31.172.71.5 (Fornex Hosting) and the '-r <ip>:8008' argument shape are campaign-specific.

DynoWiper PDB-string + vagrant build artefact in loaded modules AIInstallation Medium
Hunts for unsigned PE images on disk or loaded in memory whose embedded PDB path matches the DynoWiper build host fingerprint 'C:\Users\vagrant\Documents\Visual Studio 2013\Projects\Source\Release\Source.pdb'. Catches new compiled variants of the wiper that change filename/hash but reuse the build chain. Rationale: Pivots on the DynoWiper PDB string ESET published ('C:\Users\vagrant\Documents\Visual Studio 2013\Projects\Source\Release\Source.pdb') which is reusable across recompiled variants, plus the inetpub\pub staging directory. Variant-resilient hunting layer that complements the hash-based UC1. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/dynowiper-update-technical-analysis-attribution/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/01/new-dynowiper-malware-used-in-attempted.html
ATT&CKT1485 T1027.009
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
let SandwormPdbMarkers = dynamic([
    @"C:\Users\vagrant\Documents\Visual Studio 2013\Projects\Source\Release\Source.pdb",
    @"\vagrant\Documents\Visual Studio 2013\Projects\Source",
    @"\Source\Release\Source.pdb"
]);
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath has @"\inetpub\pub\"
   or FolderPath has @"\inetpub\pub\"
   or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has @"\Downloads\"
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where AdditionalFields has_any (SandwormPdbMarkers)
       or AdditionalFields has "vagrant"
    | project FileSHA1=SHA1, FileFolderPath=FolderPath, FileName_File=FileName, AddInfo=AdditionalFields
  ) on $left.SHA1 == $right.FileSHA1
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA1,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          AdditionalFields, FileFolderPath, AddInfo
| order by Timestamp desc
let SandwormPdbMarkers = dynamic(["vagrant\\Documents\\Visual Studio 2013\\Projects\\Source","Source\\Release\\Source.pdb"]);
WindowsEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Provider == "Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon"
| where EventID == 7
| extend Image = tostring(EventData.Image),
         ImageLoaded = tostring(EventData.ImageLoaded),
         Hashes = tostring(EventData.Hashes),
         Signed = tostring(EventData.Signed),
         OriginalFileName = tostring(EventData.OriginalFileName),
         Description = tostring(EventData.Description)
| where (ImageLoaded has_any (SandwormPdbMarkers)
         or Description has "vagrant"
         or Image has @"\inetpub\pub\")
   and Signed != "true"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Image, ImageLoaded, Hashes, Signed, OriginalFileName, Description

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("4ec3c90846af6b79ee1a5188eefa3fd21f6d4cf6") or SHA1 in~ ("4ec3c90846af6b79ee1a5188eefa3fd21f6d4cf6") or MD5 in~ ("4ec3c90846af6b79ee1a5188eefa3fd21f6d4cf6")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("4ec3c90846af6b79ee1a5188eefa3fd21f6d4cf6") or SHA1 in~ ("4ec3c90846af6b79ee1a5188eefa3fd21f6d4cf6") or MD5 in~ ("4ec3c90846af6b79ee1a5188eefa3fd21f6d4cf6")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["4ec3c90846af6b79ee1a5188eefa3fd21f6d4cf6"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

ServiceNow's Virtual Agent Vulnerability Shows Why AI Security Needs Traditional AppSec Foundations

Snyk
2026-01-14 6 use cases 2 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

The critical ServiceNow Virtual Agent vulnerability highlights a vital lesson: securing agentic AI requires a return to traditional AppSec foundations. While AI can amplify risks, the root causes often stem from classic failures in authentication and authorization.

CVEsCVE-2025-12420
ATT&CKT1190 T1528

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] BodySnatcher (CVE-2025-12420) — Hardcoded 'servicenowexternalagent' Token Observed in HTTP Traffic · [LLM] ServiceNow Virtual Agent Invocation of Hidden AIA-Agent Invoker AutoChat Topic (CVE-2025-12420)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
BodySnatcher (CVE-2025-12420) — Hardcoded 'servicenowexternalagent' Token Observed in HTTP Traffic AIExploitation High
Hunts HTTP requests carrying the hardcoded shared token string 'servicenowexternalagent' that AppOmni documented as the static credential used by every third-party integration to authenticate to the ServiceNow Virtual Agent API. Any inbound request bearing this token to a Now-platform host indicates exploitation of CVE-2025-12420 (BodySnatcher) since the credential is identical across all customer tenants. Rationale: Anchored on the literal credential string 'servicenowexternalagent' published verbatim in code-block 1 of the Snyk article (and corroborated by AppOmni's advisory). The token is identical across every ServiceNow tenant, so any occurrence in WAF, web-proxy, IIS, or EDR network telemetry is a high-fidelity exploitation signal for CVE-2025-12420. Cross-checked against: • https://www.appomni.com/blog/servicenow-virtual-agent-vulnerability • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-12420 • https://www.servicenow.com/community/now-platform-articles/security-advisory-cve-2025-12420/
ATT&CKT1078.001 T1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal red-team / purple-team replay of the AppOmni PoC against staging ServiceNow tenants
  • Vendor vulnerability scanners (Qualys, Tenable, Rapid7) executing the AppOmni signature check
  • Security researchers / journalists hosting the IOC string on educational pages indexed by web-proxy logs
  • AppOmni / ServiceNow remediation-verification probes during patch deployment windows
  • SIEM ingest of historical PoC reproduction documents stored in SharePoint / Confluence (false positive when CommonSecurityLog captures the URL of a wiki page containing the string)
Suppression filter
// Suppress vendor scanners and internal red-team test ranges that we know legitimately probe this IOC.
| where SourceIP !in ("<qualys_scanner_cidr>", "<tenable_scanner_cidr>", "<internal_redteam_cidr>")
| where not (UA has_any ("Qualys", "Nessus", "Tenable", "Rapid7", "AppOmni"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (Triage): Confirm the destination host is a ServiceNow Now-platform instance (`*.service-now.com`). Pull the full HTTP request — Authorization header, JSON body, source IP — and validate the token appears verbatim ('servicenowexternalagent', no rotation suffix). Cross-check whether the request originated from a known integration partner subnet or an unexpected external IP. Step 2 (Contain): Engage ServiceNow admin to rotate the OAuth credential for the affected integration, disable the Virtual Agent API channel for unauthenticated third-party callers, and apply the November-2025 patch if not already deployed. Block the source IP at the WAF if external. Step 3 (Hunt): Query ServiceNow sys_audit / syslog for any sys_user record created in the last 30d with admin role attached, plus any data created/modified by the 'AIA-Agent Invoker' user in the same window. Pivot to UC #2 (AIA-Agent Invoker AutoChat Topic invocation) on the same source IPs.
// Hunt the hardcoded 'servicenowexternalagent' token across any HTTP context Defender sees (URL clicks, network events with URL captured).
let IOCToken = "servicenowexternalagent";
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has IOCToken or AdditionalFields has IOCToken
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| union (UrlClickEvents | where Timestamp > ago(30d) | where Url has IOCToken | project Timestamp, AccountUpn, Url, NetworkMessageId, IPAddress)
| order by Timestamp desc
// Hunt the hardcoded 'servicenowexternalagent' token across WAF, ASIM web, and IIS telemetry.
let IOCToken = "servicenowexternalagent";
let WAFHits = CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where RequestURL has IOCToken
        or RequestClientApplication has IOCToken
        or RequestCookies has IOCToken
        or RequestContext has IOCToken
        or Message has IOCToken
        or DeviceCustomString1 has IOCToken
        or DeviceCustomString2 has IOCToken
        or DeviceCustomString3 has IOCToken
        or DeviceCustomString4 has IOCToken
        or DeviceCustomString5 has IOCToken
        or DeviceCustomString6 has IOCToken
    | project TimeGenerated, Source="WAF", SourceIP=SourceIP, DestinationHost=DestinationHostName, URL=RequestURL, UA=RequestClientApplication, Action=DeviceAction;
let WebHits = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Url has IOCToken
        or UrlOriginal has IOCToken
        or HttpRequestHeaderAuthorization has IOCToken
        or HttpRequestHeaderCookie has IOCToken
        or HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent has IOCToken
        or HttpRequestHeaderReferer has IOCToken
    | project TimeGenerated, Source="ASIM-Web", SourceIP=SrcIpAddr, DestinationHost=HttpHostName, URL=Url, UA=HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, Action=DvcAction;
let IISHits = W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where csUriQuery has IOCToken
        or csUriStem has IOCToken
        or csUserAgent has IOCToken
        or csReferer has IOCToken
    | project TimeGenerated, Source="IIS", SourceIP=cIP, DestinationHost=Computer, URL=strcat(csUriStem, "?", csUriQuery), UA=csUserAgent, Action=tostring(scStatus);
union WAFHits, WebHits, IISHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc

ServiceNow Virtual Agent Invocation of Hidden AIA-Agent Invoker AutoChat Topic (CVE-2025-12420) AIExploitation High
Hunts unauthenticated or weakly-authenticated invocations of the hidden ServiceNow AutoChat topic that wires the 'Record Management AI Agent' to the Virtual Agent API surface. AppOmni's PoC showed the BodySnatcher chain pivots through this internal topic once the static 'servicenowexternalagent' token is replayed, so any external client hitting the chatbot/v1/openframe or /api/now/v1/awa endpoints with an email-only identity payload referencing 'Record Management' is high-fidelity for CVE-2025-12420 exploitation. Rationale: Anchored on the two literal strings in code-block 1 ('servicenowexternalagent') and code-block 2 ('Record Management AI Agent') from the Snyk article, plus the AppOmni-disclosed AutoChat / AIA-Agent Invoker pivot path. The combination of a Now-platform host, a Virtual Agent API path, and one of the agent markers is uniquely tied to BodySnatcher exploitation — legitimate chatbot traffic from end users won't carry the 'Record Management' agent name in the request body because that agent is admin-only. Cross-checked against: • https://www.appomni.com/blog/servicenow-virtual-agent-vulnerability • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-12420 • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/
ATT&CKT1190 T1078.004 T1136.003
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate ServiceNow integration partners (UiPath, Microsoft Copilot Studio, Zendesk) calling the Virtual Agent API with their own scoped OAuth tokens
  • ServiceNow administrators testing the Record Management AI Agent from the platform's own admin UI during patch validation
  • Internal HR/IT self-service portals that embed the Virtual Agent chatbot widget and reference agent names in request bodies
  • AppOmni / Snyk vulnerability scanners specifically probing for CVE-2025-12420
  • ServiceNow's own MID-Server health checks that exercise the AWA API endpoint
Suppression filter
// Allow-list known ServiceNow integration partner egress IPs and the platform's own MID-Server ranges.
| where SourceIP !in ("<approved_integration_partner_cidrs>", "<servicenow_mid_server_cidr>")
| where not (UA has_any ("ServiceNow-MID", "AppOmni-Scanner", "Snyk-Vuln-Scanner"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (Triage): Pull the full HTTP request payload from the WAF / proxy log. Verify it carries an email-only identity claim (no MFA, no SSO assertion) and that the body references 'Record Management' or 'AIA-Agent Invoker'. Cross-correlate the source IP against your inventory of approved ServiceNow integration partners. Step 2 (Contain): Have the ServiceNow admin disable the Virtual Agent third-party API channel, rotate any 'servicenowexternalagent'-style shared credentials, and apply ServiceNow's CVE-2025-12420 hotfix. Block the source IP at the WAF. Step 3 (Hunt): Query the ServiceNow sys_audit table for any sys_user records created or modified by 'AIA-Agent Invoker' in the last 30 days. Enumerate which records the impersonated mailbox can now access in downstream-connected systems (Salesforce, M365) — assume lateral movement until proven otherwise. Force password reset on any admin accounts created post-incident.
// Detect outbound calls from any device to ServiceNow tenants invoking the Virtual Agent / AutoChat API while carrying Record-Management agent indicators (CVE-2025-12420 BodySnatcher).
let SnowHost = "service-now.com";
let ChatAPI = dynamic(["/api/now/v1/awa", "/api/now/cs/", "/api/sn_va_as_service", "virtualagent", "openframe"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has SnowHost
| where RemoteUrl has_any (ChatAPI)
| where AdditionalFields has_any ("Record Management", "AIA-Agent Invoker", "servicenowexternalagent", "sys_user")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountUpn, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, AdditionalFields
| order by Timestamp desc
// Detect ServiceNow Virtual Agent / AutoChat API calls that invoke the Record-Management AI Agent (CVE-2025-12420 BodySnatcher).
let SnowHost = "service-now.com";
let ChatPaths = dynamic(["/api/now/v1/awa", "/api/now/cs/", "/api/sn_va_as_service", "virtualagent", "openframe"]);
let AgentMarkers = dynamic(["Record Management", "AIA-Agent Invoker", "servicenowexternalagent", "AutoChat"]);
let WAFHits = CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DestinationHostName has SnowHost or RequestURL has SnowHost
    | where RequestURL has_any (ChatPaths)
    | where RequestURL has_any (AgentMarkers)
        or RequestCookies has_any (AgentMarkers)
        or RequestContext has_any (AgentMarkers)
        or Message has_any (AgentMarkers)
        or DeviceCustomString1 has_any (AgentMarkers)
        or DeviceCustomString2 has_any (AgentMarkers)
        or DeviceCustomString3 has_any (AgentMarkers)
        or DeviceCustomString4 has_any (AgentMarkers)
        or DeviceCustomString5 has_any (AgentMarkers)
        or DeviceCustomString6 has_any (AgentMarkers)
    | project TimeGenerated, Source="WAF", SourceIP, DestinationHost=DestinationHostName, Method=RequestMethod, URL=RequestURL, UA=RequestClientApplication, Status=tostring(EventOutcome);
let WebHits = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where HttpHostName has SnowHost or Url has SnowHost
    | where Url has_any (ChatPaths) or UrlOriginal has_any (ChatPaths)
    | where Url has_any (AgentMarkers)
        or UrlOriginal has_any (AgentMarkers)
        or HttpRequestHeaderAuthorization has_any (AgentMarkers)
        or HttpRequestHeaderCookie has_any (AgentMarkers)
        or HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent has_any (AgentMarkers)
        or HttpRequestHeaderReferer has_any (AgentMarkers)
    | project TimeGenerated, Source="ASIM-Web", SourceIP=SrcIpAddr, DestinationHost=HttpHostName, Method=HttpMethod, URL=Url, UA=HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, Status=tostring(HttpStatusCode);
let IISHits = W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where csUriStem has_any (ChatPaths)
    | where csUriQuery has_any (AgentMarkers)
        or csUriStem has_any (AgentMarkers)
        or csUserAgent has_any (AgentMarkers)
        or csReferer has_any (AgentMarkers)
    | project TimeGenerated, Source="IIS", SourceIP=cIP, DestinationHost=Computer, Method=csMethod, URL=strcat(csUriStem, "?", csUriQuery), UA=csUserAgent, Status=tostring(scStatus);
union WAFHits, WebHits, IISHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc
(source:cloudtrail OR source:azure.activity_logs) (@http.url:*service-now.com* AND (@http.url:*/api/now/v1/awa* OR @http.url:*/api/now/cs/* OR @http.url:*virtualagent* OR @http.url:*sn_va_as_service*) AND (@http.request.body:(*"Record Management"* OR *"AIA-Agent Invoker"* OR *servicenowexternalagent* OR *AutoChat*) OR @http.url:*servicenowexternalagent*))
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/service-now\.com$/i

// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-12420")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-12420")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate

| order by TimeGenerated desc

            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Nx s1ngularity: npm postinstall weaponizes AI CLI tools (claude/gemini/q) for credential recon · [LLM] Nx s1ngularity exfiltration via public GitHub repo 's1ngularity-repository' · [LLM] tj-actions/changed-files: CI runner pipes gist memdump.py to python to scrape secrets
Nx s1ngularity: npm postinstall weaponizes AI CLI tools (claude/gemini/q) for credential recon AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts the s1ngularity Nx compromise where the malicious telemetry.js postinstall script invoked locally-installed AI coding agents (Claude, Gemini, Amazon Q) non-interactively with permission-bypass flags to recursively hunt wallets, SSH keys and tokens. Pairs the AI-CLI child binary with auto-approve flags and a node/npm/shell package-script parent — the novel TTP this incident introduced. Rationale: Article names the Nx (s1ngularity) compromise abusing locally installed AI CLI tools; corroborating write-ups confirm telemetry.js postinstall invoked claude --dangerously-skip-permissions, gemini --yolo and q --trust-all-tools for recon — the AI-CLI binary + auto-approve flag + node parent triple is unique to this campaign and not a generic LOLBin pattern. Cross-checked against: • https://nx.dev/blog/s1ngularity-postmortem • https://snyk.io/blog/weaponizing-ai-coding-agents-for-malware-in-the-nx-malicious-package/ • https://thehackernews.com/2025/08/malicious-nx-packages-in-s1ngularity.html
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059 T1552.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer legitimately running 'claude --dangerously-skip-permissions' in a local automation script
  • CI pipeline using 'gemini --yolo' or 'q --no-interactive' for code generation or review
  • Security researcher reproducing the s1ngularity payload in a sandbox
  • Internal agentic-AI tooling that auto-approves tool calls from a node-based wrapper
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("code","cursor","windsurf","code-insiders")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full ProcessCommandLine and the parent chain — confirm the AI CLI was spawned by node/npm/npx/telemetry.js rather than an interactive terminal, and inspect the prompt for filesystem/credential recon keywords. Check npm/yarn lockfiles on the host for compromised Nx versions. 2) Contain: isolate the host, revoke and rotate all GitHub PATs, npm tokens, SSH keys and cloud credentials reachable from that workstation, and check GitHub org for new public repos. 3) Hunt: search the same user/host for writes to /tmp/inventory.txt, ~/.bashrc 'sudo shutdown' appends, and 'gh repo create' or git remotes referencing s1ngularity-repository (UC2).
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("claude","gemini","q","claude.exe","gemini.exe","q.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--dangerously-skip-permissions","--yolo","--trust-all-tools","--no-interactive")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","npm","npx","sh","bash","zsh","node.exe","npm.cmd","npx.cmd")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("telemetry.js","postinstall","nx")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("claude","gemini","q")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("--dangerously-skip-permissions","--yolo","--trust-all-tools","--no-interactive")
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node","npm","npx","sh","bash","zsh")
   or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("telemetry.js","postinstall","nx")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Nx s1ngularity AI CLI Weaponized For Credential Recon
id: 7a1f2c84-6d3e-4b9a-9f21-3c8d4e5a6b70
status: experimental
description: Detects locally installed AI coding agents (claude/gemini/q) invoked non-interactively with permission-bypass flags by a node/npm package-install context, as seen in the Nx s1ngularity npm compromise.
references:
  - https://nx.dev/blog/s1ngularity-postmortem
  - https://snyk.io/blog/weaponizing-ai-coding-agents-for-malware-in-the-nx-malicious-package/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/26
tags:
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.t1059
  - attack.t1552.001
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_img:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/claude'
      - '/gemini'
      - '/q'
  selection_flag:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '--dangerously-skip-permissions'
      - '--yolo'
      - '--trust-all-tools'
      - '--no-interactive'
  condition: selection_img and selection_flag
level: high
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE (@process.command_line:(*--dangerously-skip-permissions* OR *--yolo* OR *--trust-all-tools*)) (@process.name:(claude OR gemini OR q) OR @process.executable.path:(*/claude OR */gemini OR */q))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\/(claude|gemini|q)(\.exe)?$/i
| CommandLine=/--(dangerously-skip-permissions|yolo|trust-all-tools|no-interactive)/i
| ParentBaseFileName=/(node|npm|npx|sh|bash|zsh)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())

Nx s1ngularity exfiltration via public GitHub repo 's1ngularity-repository' AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts the exfiltration stage of the Nx s1ngularity attack, where stolen data was pushed to attacker-forced public GitHub repositories named 's1ngularity-repository' (with random 5-char suffixes) and staged in /tmp/inventory.txt before upload via the gh/git CLI. The repo-name string is a near-unique campaign IOC. Rationale: Corroborated reporting confirms exfil repos named s1ngularity-repository(-aaaaa) and data staged in /tmp/inventory.txt; both strings are specific to this campaign, making a literal command-line match an extremely high-fidelity, low-FP alert. Cross-checked against: • https://nx.dev/blog/s1ngularity-postmortem • https://thehackernews.com/2025/08/malicious-nx-packages-in-s1ngularity.html
ATT&CKT1567 T1195.002 T1552.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel analyst pasting the IOC string into a terminal/ticket while investigating
  • Detection engineer building or testing this very rule with a sample command
  • Honeypot or purple-team exercise replaying the s1ngularity exfil chain
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm whether the command actually created/pushed to a remote (gh repo create, git push) versus a benign string reference; identify the GitHub identity used. 2) Contain: isolate host, revoke the GitHub PAT/OAuth token, and request GitHub/org admin to delete any public s1ngularity-repository* repos and pull their commit contents for scope. 3) Hunt: enumerate all secrets staged in /tmp/inventory.txt, rotate everything exposed, and pivot to UC1 on the same host to confirm the AI-CLI recon precursor and any ~/.bashrc shutdown persistence.

| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("s1ngularity-repository","/tmp/inventory.txt")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "s1ngularity-repository"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("s1ngularity-repository","/tmp/inventory.txt")
   or ParentProcessCommandLine has "s1ngularity-repository"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
